---
id: "smk-17"
title: "Atlantic puffin"
---

The Atlantic puffin is a seabird of the auk family that breeds on coasts and islands of the North Atlantic, from Maine and Newfoundland to Iceland, Norway and the British Isles. It is a small, stocky bird with black upper parts, white underparts, grey cheeks and, in the breeding season, a large, brightly coloured orange, yellow and blue-grey bill that gives it a comical appearance. Puffins nest in burrows dug into grassy cliff tops, where each pair raises a single chick. They feed on small fish such as sand eels, which they catch by swimming under water using their wings, and a parent can carry many fish crosswise in its bill at once. Outside the breeding season puffins spend the winter far out at sea. Some colonies have declined because of warming seas and shortages of prey fish, and the species is listed as vulnerable in Europe.
